title: The impact of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) on open-label placebo effects
summary:
Studies have shown that placebos can be effective even when participants are aware that they are receiving an inactive substance. These so-called open-label placebos have been demonstrated to influence pain perception and subjective stress experience. However, the underlying mechanisms of these effects remain unclear.
This study aims to examine the strength of these effects and whether they differ between healthy individuals and individuals with depression. Additionally, it investigates whether the effects of an open-label placebo on stress and pain perception can be enhanced by non-invasive brain stimulation using direct current.
The study consists of two sessions. One group of participants openly receives a placebo (nasal spray), while a control group also receives a nasal spray, but without it being described as a placebo. In both cases, the nasal sprays only contain water. In one of the sessions, participants receive additional active brain stimulation, and in the other session inactive stimulation. Participants do not know in which session they receive the active or inactive stimulation. After receiving the nasal spray, participants complete various tasks on a computer.

interventions.name:
Healthy participants
Intervention: Open-label placebo (nasal spray), described as a placebo
Two test sessions, 4–10 days apart
Each session combined with either active or sham tDCS over the DLPFC (order randomized)

Healthy participants
Intervention: Nasal spray, presented as “to improve physiological measurements” 
Two test sessions, 4–10 days apart
Each session combined with either active or sham tDCS over the DLPFC (order randomized)

Participants diagnosed with a depressive disorder or episode
Intervention: Open-label placebo (nasal spray), described as a placebo
Two test sessions, 4–10 days apart
Each session combined with either active or sham tDCS over the DLPFC (order randomized)

Participants diagnosed with a depressive disorder/episode
Intervention: Nasal spray, presented as “to improve physiological measurements” (cover story)
Two test sessions, 4–10 days apart
Each session combined with either active or sham tDCS over the DLPFC (order randomized)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed depression or depressive disorder
Exclusion criteria:
- Brain injury, metal in the head, or implants
- Substance abuse or excessive alcohol consumption
- Epilepsy
